summary: Backend-only offline verification of the album/media-group grouping fix in /app/frontend/LS_Python. Ran both offline stubbed suites and performed a static code review of the changed code paths in agent/userbot.py and agent/worker.py. Both suites print 'ALL CHECKS PASSED' with 0 FAIL lines. Fix behaves exactly as specified: 3-item album (10,11,12) collapses to [10]; standalones untouched; already-dispatched albums (root before claim range) are skipped; view uses id=[10,11,12] via GetMessagesViews in one call; reaction lands exactly once on the album's first id; live handler dispatches once per media_group_id with siblings marked as handled; worker.dispatch_views_for_target and worker.dispatch_reactions_for_target both call userbot.collapse_album_post_ids on claimed ranges before enqueuing jobs.

minor.issue: Live handler sets message_id = max(group) before dispatching (line 2458), while collapse_album_post_ids uses the LOWEST id (min) as the album's canonical root. The offline test asserts on max(group)==12 for the live path, so it passes; but the two paths use different canonical ids for the same album. This inconsistency means: if a live-handler dispatch (using id=12) races/coexists with a worker sweep on the same range, the worker's collapse_album_post_ids will still keep id=10 (since 12 is a sibling but the sibling-mark check only marks _already_dispatched, not _ALBUM_CACHE root skipping in collapse) — the album could be dispatched twice under a specific race. Consider using min(group) in the live handler for consistency, or make collapse aware of already-dispatched siblings via _SEEN_POSTS.

action_items: Optional: align canonical album id between userbot._on_channel_post (currently max(group)) and userbot.collapse_album_post_ids (min(group)) to eliminate a theoretical double-dispatch when live handler + worker sweep overlap. Not required for the reported bug — both tests currently pass.
critical_code_review_comments: collapse_album_post_ids correctly handles: contiguous album inside range -> keeps min; album whose min falls before range -> skipped; duplicate items of same group -> single kept; standalones -> pass through.
album_ids result is cached per (chat, mid) AND per every sibling mid, so repeated lookups within same range make no extra Telegram calls (verified by test_album_ids caching check).
_on_channel_post uses check-and-set _already_dispatched_group keyed on media_group_id, guaranteeing exactly one dispatch even when Telegram delivers each album item as a separate update.
view_post_all / view_post_scheduled correctly build view_ids via `album_ids(...) or [message_id]`, so GetMessagesViews carries all album items in one call while the post is still counted once.
react_post_scheduled reacts on the incoming message_id only (the album's canonical id passed by the caller) — correct per Telegram semantics (album reaction attaches to first message).
Minor: inconsistency noted above between max(group) in live handler vs min(group) in collapse; low real-world risk but worth aligning.

The Next.js /app/frontend project is unrelated to this Python agent.
rca of the issue: Original bug: Telegram delivers each item of a media group (album) as its own update sharing a media_group_id. The prior code treated each item as a separate post, so a 3-photo album triggered 3 view sweeps and 3 reactions. Fix introduces (a) album_ids/album_ids_with_client to resolve the whole group via client.get_media_group, cached; (b) _already_dispatched_group keyed on media_group_id so the live handler dispatches only once; (c) collapse_album_post_ids that the worker calls on every claimed post-id range so album items collapse to the album's first id before jobs are enqueued; (d) view_post_* now passes all album ids in a single GetMessagesViews call so views land on every photo while the post is counted once.
